```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea B has no gating regulatory steps. Idea A's own brief lists an IRS EFIN application with a suitability check and EA/attorney review, annual IRS software acceptance testing, and pre-launch EU data-protection counsel. Any of these could push a first paid filing past 90 days for one person.",
    "Idea B's scope is thin and shippable: upload, OTP/SSO and a directory. Idea A's stated differentiator, filing the country-of-residence return as well, requires liability-bearing tax logic per jurisdiction on top of PFIC/FBAR. Even the most sophisticated competitor in A's brief calls the local side 'the hard part' and does not solve it.",
    "Idea B has sourced, monetizing precedents for the exact product at low price points: display.dev at €15–€49/mo and Volly at $75/mo per workspace. Landing one paying customer at $15–75/mo is a low bar.",
    "Idea B's acquisition channels are cheap or free and fit the buyer: Product Hunt at roughly $3–5 CPA, Show HN at $0, and free Claude/MCP marketplace listings. Idea A relies on Meta lead-gen, where the brief itself says CPL in finance runs above the $27.66 blended average, against a one-time $150–$300 sale.",
    "Idea A's US-only fallback is crowded and commoditized. Six self-serve competitors charge $67–$219, so retreating to the US-side problem to meet the timeline removes the wedge."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A has no evidence that anyone wants or will pay for a combined US + country-of-residence product, which is the idea's whole differentiator. All three Reddit quotes describe pain with US-side forms and accountant fees. The Atamatax line is competitor commentary, not buyer demand. The 'case for' claim that Atamatax 'attract[s] customers' at $199–$799 cites only a pricing page, with no customer or revenue evidence. Willingness to pay for the combined product is listed as an open question.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-low. Idea B's independent demand evidence is also thin: one vendor-curated testimonial, plus one Reddit post about sharing tools rather than paying for hosting. B also has five near-identical competitors, no clear wedge, and a real sandbox-security liability. B wins mainly because Idea A's regulatory and multi-jurisdiction scope makes a paying customer within 90 days unlikely, not because B's demand is proven."
}
```
